samples.summary: Enter at offset 0 of a non-empty bulleted heading strands the remembered level on the empty leading bullet and drops it from the text
samples.evidence: `Doc.splitBlock` (document.ts:330) chooses `newType = 'list-item'` for any non-empty list-item, and `applySplitBlock` deletes `after.headingLevel` for every non-`heading` half (block-helpers.ts:256-258). Pressing Enter at offset 0 of a bulleted Heading 2 therefore leaves the *empty* first half carrying `headingLevel: 2` while the half that actually holds the heading text loses it. Un-bulleting afterwards produces an empty Heading 2 above a body-text bullet — the inverse of what the user sees. The design note (docs/design/docs/docs.md:172-177) only reasons about splitting at the end, not at offset 0, and the new test suite only covers the end-of-text split (list-heading-roundtrip.test.ts:176-190).

samples.summary: The remembered heading level is invisible while bulleted, so identical-looking bullets un-bullet to different block types
samples.evidence: `blockStyleId` (named-styles.ts:99-113) and layout (`layout.ts:150`, `layout.ts:933`) resolve a `list-item` to the `normal` style regardless of the retained `headingLevel`, so a bulleted Heading 2 renders exactly like a bulleted paragraph. `unlistedBlockType` (types.ts:336-343) then makes those two visually identical bullets exit the list as different block types (Heading 2 vs paragraph) with no on-screen cue, including for bullets a user never knowingly created from a heading (e.g. typing `- ` on a heading, text-editor.ts:2319). Google Docs avoids this by *rendering* the bulleted heading as a heading.

samples.summary: `unlistedBlockType` restores `heading` but not `title`/`subtitle`, so bulleting a Title silently flattens it
samples.evidence: `unlistedBlockType` only remembers `headingLevel`; `MemDocStore.setBlockType` (memory.ts:257-263) and the Yorkie store (yorkie-doc-store.ts:1394) likewise only preserve `headingLevel` for a `list-item`. Bulleting a `title` or `subtitle` block (both real BlockTypes handled by `blockStyleId` at named-styles.ts:101-104) and then un-bulleting returns `paragraph`, permanently downgrading the block — the same class of loss this change fixes for headings, left unhandled. No preservation of the previous `title`/`subtitle` type exists on any store path.

finding.summary: Heading memory propagates to every sibling bullet on split, so un-bulleting a list started from a heading turns plain body items into headings
finding.evidence: `applySplitBlock` now keeps `after.headingLevel` when `newBlockType === 'list-item'` (block-helpers.ts:260-262), and `Doc.splitBlock` (document.ts:330-331) always uses `newType = 'list-item'` when splitting a list item. So: bullet a Heading 2 → Enter at end → the new, empty bullet also carries `headingLevel: 2` → the user types body text ("revenue up") in it. Selecting the whole list and toggling the bullet off (editor.ts:2869-2872 → `unlistedBlockType`) now converts EVERY item, including the pure body-text ones, into Heading 2. The memory should arguably only ride along on a mid-text split of the original bulleted heading, not onto freshly created empty siblings. The new test at test/view/list-heading-roundtrip.test.ts:189-207 locks in exactly this propagation, so nothing catches it.

verdict.reason: The described code does not exist. The finding claims applySplitBlock preserves `after.headingLevel` when `newBlockType === 'list-item'` at block-helpers.ts:260-262. In fact block-helpers.ts:256-258 reads `if (newBlockType !== 'heading') { delete after.headingLevel; }` — since Doc.splitBlock passes 'list-item' for a list-item split (document.ts:330-331), and 'list-item' !== 'heading', headingLevel is unconditionally DELETED on the new block. Lines 260-262 are the listKind/listLevel preservation block and never mention headingLevel. memory.ts:226-231, the only store consumer of applySplitBlock, does not re-add headingLevel. Therefore a fresh empty sibling bullet created by Enter cannot carry headingLevel: 2, and unlistedBlockType can never promote a body-text sibling to a heading. The cited test is also the opposite of what the finding says it locks in: list-heading-roundtrip.test.ts:174-189 is titled 'splitting a bulleted heading leaves the new bullet plain' and asserts `expect(second.headingLevel).toBeUndefined()` (line 185) plus exit to 'paragraph' (line 188), with a comment at 179-180 stating the exact invariant the finding alleges is violated. The propagation mechanism is not present.
